prs.author: keurcien

prs.author: Dharit13

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address the same root cause: the write_stream memory object stream is created with buffer_size=0 (fully synchronous rendezvous), which causes send_stream.send() to block until stdout_writer has fully flushed the previous message to stdout. When a handler sends a progress notification followed immediately by its final response, the response send blocks/serializes behind the notification's I/O, which can stall certain request/notification interleavings. (2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py aggressively JSON-decodes string parameter values for any annotation that isn't exactly `str`, which corrupts plain string inputs that happen to look like JSON (e.g. a literal string payload) when the field type is a union that includes `str` alongside other simple types such as `str | None`. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py aggressively JSON-decodes string parameter values for any annotation that isn't exactly `str`, which corrupts plain string inputs that happen to look like JSON (e.g. a literal string payload) when the field type is a union that includes `str` alongside other simple types such as `str | None`. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 narrowly special-cases `str | None` (Optional[str]) and documents why that specific union is safe to exempt from pre-parsing (no other member of the union can legitimately result from decoding a JSON string), and it explicitly unwraps `Annotated[...]` on both the outer annotation and each union member before checking, so `Annotated[str | None, Field(...)]`-style params (the idiomatic way to add a description) are covered. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead skips pre-parsing for ANY union composed solely of {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - e.g. `int | str` or `bool | str` - which changes coercion behavior for those unions too (not just the reported str-corruption case) and does not unwrap `Annotated` at the top level via `get_origin`, so an `Annotated`-wrapped union annotation falls through to the `return True` branch and the fix silently doesn't apply in that common case.

clusters.pick_reason: #3056 narrowly special-cases `str | None` (Optional[str]) and documents why that specific union is safe to exempt from pre-parsing (no other member of the union can legitimately result from decoding a JSON string), and it explicitly unwraps `Annotated[...]` on both the outer annotation and each union member before checking, so `Annotated[str | None, Field(...)]`-style params (the idiomatic way to add a description) are covered. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead skips pre-parsing for ANY union composed solely of {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - e.g. `int | str` or `bool | str` - which changes coercion behavior for those unions too (not just the reported str-corruption case) and does not unwrap `Annotated` at the top level via `get_origin`, so an `Annotated`-wrapped union annotation falls through to the `return True` branch and the fix silently doesn't apply in that common case.

members.author: yaowubarbara

clusters.pick_reason: 2395 fixes the hang at its source: it sends a scoped JSONRPCError (matching the pending request's id) directly onto ctx.read_stream_writer, resolving only the specific in-flight request that was waiting on the dropped stream, and guards with an isinstance(JSONRPCRequest) check so notifications aren't affected. 3098's approach instead raises a StreamableHTTPError and adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull it back out of an anyio ExceptionGroup — implying the failure propagates through the TaskGroup and tears down the broader session/task group rather than resolving just the affected request, a larger blast radius for the same fix. 3098's diff also carries an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`), suggesting a less isolated patch.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara

clusters.pick_reason: 2395 fixes the hang at its source: it sends a scoped JSONRPCError (matching the pending request's id) directly onto ctx.read_stream_writer, resolving only the specific in-flight request that was waiting on the dropped stream, and guards with an isinstance(JSONRPCRequest) check so notifications aren't affected. 3098's approach instead raises a StreamableHTTPError and adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull it back out of an anyio ExceptionGroup — implying the failure propagates through the TaskGroup and tears down the broader session/task group rather than resolving just the affected request, a larger blast radius for the same fix. 3098's diff also carries an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`), suggesting a less isolated patch.
